source: Minchat Shai on Gen 11:5 (Ramah; Masorah at Bo)
claim_en: וירד ה' לראת ("and the LORD came down TO SEE") — the Ramah: the see-infinitive is plene throughout the Torah EXCEPT THREE defective — the land that cannot BE SEEN under the locusts (Exod 10:5), God's descent TO SEE the tower (here), and "you cannot SEE My face" (Exod 33:20). SNAPSHOT: exactly those three defective, all others full — a trio about the limits of seeing, each missing a letter.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 11:3 (final-letter cipher)
claim_en: איש אל רעהו הבה ("each to his fellow: come!") — the FINAL letters spell שלוה ("tranquility"): "from excess tranquility they sinned" (Kitzur). SNAPSHOT finals locked in verse order.

בנסעם ("as they journeyed") — the Masorah pair, both in the Torah: the Babel migration (11:2) and the camp journeying from Sinai (Num 10:34): "that day they turned from following the LORD — like a child running from school; they journeyed מקדם — from the Ancient One of the world" (Kitzur). SNAPSHOT: exactly two tokens.

ויפץ ("and He SCATTERED") — the Kitzur's trio: Babel's builders (11:8), the people scattered through Egypt for straw (Exod 5:12), and the people scattering from Saul (I Sam 13:8) — "the tower-men and Egypt deserved one punishment." Torah-side: exactly the two; the Samuel leg is an inheritance edge.

ויחדלו ("and they CEASED") — the Masorah pair, both in the Torah: they ceased building the city (11:8) and "the sounds and hail CEASED" (Exod 9:33): "teaching that these too were judged with sounds and hail" (Kitzur). SNAPSHOT: exactly two tokens.

ודברים ("and words [few]") — the Kitzur's pair leaps to Ecclesiastes: "vanities and MANY WORDS" (Eccl 5:6) — "they multiplied speaking many vanities." Torah-side: the word's only token; the Ecclesiastes leg is an inheritance edge.

לאבן ("for stone" — brick served them for stone) — the Kitzur's pair leaps to Nabal: "his heart died within him and he became STONE" (I Sam 25:37) — "as there a death, so here: harder to them than death was a brick falling from the tower." Torah-side: the word's only token; the Samuel leg is an inheritance edge.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 11:2 (Ben Asher; precise books)
claim_en: וימצאו ("and they found [a valley]") — the vav with the lengthening stroke (maarikh) "per Ben Asher, and so in the precise books": SNAPSHOT's codepoints carry the stroke — Ben Asher confirmation #3.
וראשו בשמים ("its head in the heavens") — the bet SOFT (no dagesh): bet+vowel contiguous in SNAPSHOT.
בני האדם ("the sons of man" — who built) — the bet with dagesh (doubling dot). SNAPSHOT agrees.

OUR 11:7 IS A MEMBER OF THE TRANSLATION-ALTERATION CANON. The verse reads הָבָה נֵרְדָה ('COME, LET US DESCEND'), and the plural is recorded as one of the places the elders deliberately altered when rendering the Torah for the king, writing 'Come, I shall descend' in the singular to forestall a misreading. This unit's own verse therefore sits inside the corpus's documented list of translation deltas - the same canon this project's Aramaic track is read against.

check.note: A verse recorded as deliberately altered in an ancient royal translation, joining the documented alteration canon.

claim_en: THE TOWER'S STATED MOTIVE IS COSMOLOGICAL ENGINEERING, AND ITS INTERVAL IS THIS CORPUS'S OWN NUMBER. The builders are read as reasoning that every one thousand six hundred and fifty-six years the firmament collapses, so supports must be built to hold it - and that interval is precisely the year-count of the flood narrative this same span follows. The project is read as a repair against a recurrence the previous units had just demonstrated.

check.note: A motive whose stated interval equals the flood's own year-count in this corpus - an engineering rationale built on the previous units' events.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 38:6; Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Kaspa 4:5
claim_en: THE 'ONE SPEECH' OF OUR 11:1 IS PARSED FOUR WAYS, AND THE 'NAME' OF 11:4 IS READ AS IDOLATRY BY VERBAL ANALOGY. The unified speech is read as obscured deeds stated only implicitly - unlike the flood generation's explicit sins - as sharp words spoken against the oneness of God, as shared property, and as the supports scheme. And R. Natan derives that 'let us make us a NAME' means an idol, arguing by verbal analogy from the phrase 'the name of other gods'; Rebbi derives the same point in the reverse direction, from the other verse. The direction of the derivation is itself disputed.

check.note: A phrase parsed four ways, and an idolatry reading argued by verbal analogy whose DIRECTION between the two verses is disputed.

claim_en: THE PUNISHMENT IS SPLIT THREE WAYS BECAUSE THE BUILDERS ARE SPLIT THREE WAYS. R. Yirmeya bar Elazar reads three factions with three intentions - to dwell there, to worship idols, to wage war - and three different fates: dispersed, language confounded, or transformed into apes, spirits and demons. Only the second matches our 11:9's stated outcome, so the operator's recorded effect covers one faction of three. The sin itself is debated, and one proposal is refuted from this unit's own ink: they built in a VALLEY, so the answer comes back - then build on a mountain.

check.note: A single stated punishment read as covering one of three factions, with a proposed sin refuted from the unit's own topography.

source: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Shirah 5:9; Sifrei Devarim 43:9; Tosefta Sotah 3:3
claim_en: THE GRACE-PERIOD TOKEN RETURNS, AND THE CAUSE-CHAIN IS READ OFF ONE WORD. 'AND NOW' at our 11:6 is read as the opening of repentance - nothing was decreed until the evil was consummated - the same reading the corpus gives the identical token in the Eden sentence. And the cause is traced to our 11:2's SITTING, read by verbal analogy with a later verse as eating and drinking: satisfaction produced the haughtiness that produced the building.

check.note: A token read as a repentance-opening, matching the same token's reading in an earlier unit; and a cause-chain derived from a sitting-verb by verbal analogy.
